lockFileMaintenance.description: Renovate-side automerge rather than platformAutomerge: GitHub's auto-merge waits only for the required ci check, while Renovate merges only once every status on the branch is green. The release-age wait for a refresh comes from pnpm-workspace.yaml's minimumReleaseAge, not from renovate/stability-days (see the lockFileMaintenance packageRule). This still does not merge unattended: a refresh moves bundled transitive code (undici under @actions/github, say), so dist/ goes stale and CI stays red until the bundle is rebuilt and committed. Automerge fires after that lands.

packageRules.description: Auto-merge everything except svelte-vitals/@svelte-vitals/core (those need a manually-added changeset, see the 'svelte-vitals' group below) and major updates (need review) — CI (build/test/lint, including the dist-freshness check) still has to pass first. The Renovate app is on main's ruleset bypass list specifically so these can merge without a human review.

engines.node is a deliberately chosen floor, tracking the engines of the bundled svelte-vitals/@svelte-vitals/core — raised by hand when an analyzer bump raises theirs, since that is a reviewed decision rather than a version to chase. Never auto-bump it. CI runs on the latest Node 24.x via pnpm/setup's `runtime: node@24`, which needs no Renovate tracking.
Same maintainer, same trust boundary as this repo — the 3-day supply-chain wait below is for third-party deps, not our own just-published releases.

lockFileMaintenance has no release timestamp, so the default timestamp-required behaviour leaves renovate/stability-days pending forever. pnpm-workspace.yaml's minimumReleaseAge enforces the cooldown when the lockfile is regenerated. Not minimumReleaseAge: null — that stops Renovate setting the status at all, so a pending one already on the branch is never replaced.

changesets/action refuses to run against a mismatched @changesets/cli major (its v2 rejects cli v2 outright and points at action@v1), so splitting these across two PRs leaves whichever merges first with a release workflow that cannot version or publish. They arrive together and are reviewed as one change. Listed last because a later packageRule's groupName wins, and @changesets/cli would otherwise land in devDependencies.
